% SECTION 7: PROOFS OF THE CORE THEOREMS  
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%  
\section{Proofs of the Core Theorems}  
\label{sec:proofs}  
  
This section provides the complete, unabridged symbolic derivations for the core structural theorems verified by the computational and formal layers.  
  
\subsection{Complete Derivation of Theorem \ref{thm:defect_characterization}}  
We prove the equivalence loop (1) $\implies$ (3) $\implies$ (2) $\implies$ (4) $\implies$ (1).  
\begin{proof}  
$\bullet$ \textbf{(1) $\implies$ (3):} Assume $D_\Pi = Q_\Pi K P_\Pi = 0$. Substituting $Q_\Pi = I - P_\Pi$ yields $(I - P_\Pi) K P_\Pi = 0$. Distributing terms gives $K P_\Pi - P_\Pi K P_\Pi = 0$, which isolates to $K P_\Pi = P_\Pi K P_\Pi$.  
  
$\bullet$ \textbf{(3) $\implies$ (2):} Assume $K P_\Pi = P_\Pi K P_\Pi$. Let $v \in V_\Pi$ be an arbitrary vector. Since $P_\Pi$ is an orthogonal projection onto $V_\Pi$, it acts as the identity map on its target space: $P_\Pi v = v$. Evaluating the transition action: $K v = K(P_\Pi v) = (K P_\Pi) v$. Applying our hypothesis: $K v = (P_\Pi K P_\Pi) v = P_\Pi(K P_\Pi v) = P_\Pi(K v)$. Because $K v$ is invariant under $P_\Pi$, it must lie within $\text{Im}(P_\Pi) = V_\Pi$, proving $K(V_\Pi) \subseteq V_\Pi$.  
  
$\bullet$ \textbf{(2) $\implies$ (4):} Let $\Pi = \{B_1, \dots, B_m\}$. The subspace $V_\Pi$ is spanned by block indicators $\{\mathbf{1}_{B_i}\}$. Since $K(V_\Pi) \subseteq V_\Pi$, the image of each indicator must be a linear combination of block indicators: $K \mathbf{1}_{B_i} = \sum_{j=1}^m c_{ij} \mathbf{1}_{B_j}$. At the state level, summing the action over all $x \in B_i$ gives $K \mathbf{1}_{B_i} = \sum_{x \in B_i} e_{T(x)}$. Equating the expressions: $\sum_{x \in B_i} e_{T(x)} = \sum_{j=1}^m c_{ij} (\sum_{y \in B_j} e_y)$. Because $\{e_y\}$ forms an orthonormal basis, coefficients must match identically. The left side has coefficients of 1 for mapped states. For the right side to balance, $c_{ij}$ must be exactly 1 for a single target block $j^*$ and 0 otherwise, meaning $T(B_i) \subseteq B_{j^*}$ (a valid forward congruence).  
  
$\bullet$ \textbf{(4) $\implies$ (1):} Assume the partition is a forward congruence: $K \mathbf{1}_{B_i} = \mathbf{1}_{B_{j(i)}}$. Evaluating the global action on any $w \in V$, the projection is $P_\Pi w = \sum_{i=1}^m \gamma_i(w) \mathbf{1}_{B_i}$ where $\gamma_i(w) = \frac{1}{|B_i|} \sum_{x \in B_i} w_x$. Applying $K$ linearly: $K P_\Pi w = \sum_{i=1}^m \gamma_i(w) (K \mathbf{1}_{B_i}) = \sum_{i=1}^m \gamma_i(w) \mathbf{1}_{B_{j(i)}}$. Because the output is a linear combination of block indicators, $K P_\Pi w \in V_\Pi$. Applying $P_\Pi$ leaves it unchanged: $P_\Pi(K P_\Pi w) = K P_\Pi w \implies P_\Pi K P_\Pi = K P_\Pi$. Subtracting terms yields $(I - P_\Pi) K P_\Pi = 0 \implies Q_\Pi K P_\Pi = 0$, hence $D_\Pi = 0$.  
\end{proof}  
  
\subsection{Complete Derivation of Theorem 4.2 (The Commutator Fallacy)}  
\begin{proof}  
As derived in Section 4, expanding the commutator via $I = P_\Pi + Q_\Pi$ yields $[K, P_\Pi] = D_\Pi - P_\Pi K Q_\Pi$. Under the hypothesis that the defect vanishes ($D_\Pi = 0$), this reduces to $[K, P_\Pi] = - P_\Pi K Q_\Pi$. Full commutation $[K, P_\Pi] = 0$ requires the auxiliary condition $P_\Pi K Q_\Pi = 0$.   
  
The operator $Q_\Pi$ projects onto $V_\Pi^\perp = \ker(P_\Pi)$. The condition $P_\Pi K Q_\Pi = 0$ implies $P_\Pi(K w) = 0$ for all $w \in V_\Pi^\perp$, which means $K w \in V_\Pi^\perp$, forcing the complement space to be forward-invariant: $K(V_\Pi^\perp) \subseteq V_\Pi^\perp$. In finite deterministic dynamics, $V_\Pi^\perp$ represents high-frequency local fluctuations within blocks (components summing to zero over every block). For $K(V_\Pi^\perp) \subseteq V_\Pi^\perp$ to hold, the dynamics must map zero-sum fluctuation vectors to zero-sum fluctuation vectors, requiring $T$ to behave as a bijective permutation within and across blocks. If $T$ is non-invertible---such as when multiple transient states merge---local fluctuations are squashed, mapping a zero-sum vector to a non-zero-sum vector and breaking the invariance of $V_\Pi^\perp$. Thus, any system with irreversible transient merging can have $D_\Pi = 0$ while failing full commutation ($[K, P_\Pi] \neq 0$).  
\end{proof}

\section{The Tri-Certificate Verification Protocol}  
\label{sec:protocol}  
  
To ensure mathematical claims match their software implementations, AQARION replaces traditional unverified test code with a structured, three-tiered verification protocol. This methodology splits system verification into three independent layers of proof: \textbf{Mathematical}, \textbf{Computational}, and \textbf{Reproducibility} certificates.  
  
\subsection{Specification of the Verification Tiers}  
\begin{itemize}  
    \item \textbf{The Mathematical Certificate:} Evaluated inside the Lean 4 formal environment. It provides a purely deductive proof of the structural theorems (such as Theorem \ref{thm:defect_characterization}), verifying that the underlying logic contains zero unproven assumptions (\texttt{sorry}).  
    \item \textbf{The Computational Certificate:} Executed via an exact-arithmetic matrix pipeline. It performs an exhaustive evaluation of the finite state space, computing exact state counts, block partitions, defect norms, and Jordan canonical signatures without floating-point approximations.  
    \item \textbf{The Reproducibility Certificate:} Supervised by an independent rebuild engine. It enforces cross-environment bit-for-bit identity across standard platforms (Linux, macOS, and Android-Termux architectures). It guarantees that environment configurations do not alter the calculated values.  
\end{itemize}  
  
\subsection{Level 21 Semantic Invariants}  
The connection between these verification layers is defined by a strict serialization contract known as the \textbf{Level 21 Semantic Invariants}. The test harness \texttt{verify\_all.py} cannot return a generic boolean success state. Instead, it must serialize its internal calculation states using a strict, cross-kernel JSON layout matching the following properties:  
\begin{itemize}  
    \item \textbf{Canonical Ordering:} Every JSON block must recursively sort its object keys alphabetically.  
    \item \textbf{Whitespace Minimization:} Separators must be stripped of padding tokens (using compact separators \texttt{','} and \texttt{':'}).  
    \item \textbf{Encoding Invariance:} Output manifests are encoded exclusively in UTF-8 with standard line-feed (\verb|\n|) terminators.  
\end{itemize}  
This strict formatting ensures that the generated document yields a completely stable SHA-256 hash across different operating environments and independent language implementations (Python, TypeScript, and Lean 4).  
  
\subsection{The Read-Only Anchor (expected\_results.json)}  
The operational truth of the repository is anchored by \texttt{verification/expected\_results.json}. Standard continuous integration gates compare the real-time calculated values and artifact hashes directly against this frozen ledger:
